newsitem.title: UK: London gold off lows as Dow and dollar slide.
newsitem.headline: London gold off lows as Dow and dollar slide.

text.p: Gold prices pulled off their lows on Friday afternoon as tumbling U.S. stocks prompted a spate of short covering, traders said.
Around the afternoon fix, gold tried to regain levels above interim support at $325.00 an ounce, after sinking below that late on Thursday.
Bullion fixed at $324.65, compared with $323.50 in the morning but well below the $326.15 fixing from Thursday afternoon.
A stronger dollar had deflated gold the previous day but the currency had since weakened.
"The dollar came off and we saw gold looking at $326 again," a dealer said.
"And with the Dow (Jones Industrial Average) down more than 100 points we've seen some short covering by the funds in gold."

But analysts said enthusiasm for gold, locked in a steep downtrend since the start of the year, was low and more drastic Wall Street losses would be required to pull serious investor money into the metal.
The market would need to negate key resistance around $329-$330 before generating any significant upward correction, chartists noted.
Early trading in precious metals had been dull, with much of Europe closed for the Assumption Day holiday, but actitivity picked up after the New York Comex futures market opened.
In the white metals, silver followed gold modestly higher, but palladium took a hit on general selling, falling nearly $10 to test important technical support around $210.
Dealers attributed losses in part to the appearance of small volumes of Russian material on the market as well as a continued correction from 17-year highs earlier this month.
"There's been general selling. When a market is rangebound and someone picks a direction, as in palladium, everyone follows. In this case it's down," a dealer said.
But supplies were still tight and a big price drop was very unlikely, dealers said.
The market was last quoted at $208.50/$210.50, down $8.50, while platinum was indicated at $4.22/$425.50, off $2.00.
Silver followed gold and picked up moderately from early lows before stalling around $4.45.
It was last indicated at $4.43/$4.45, compared to $4.49/$4.51 at Thursday's finish.
